newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Autoliv says satisfied with 1997 so far.
newsitem.headline: Autoliv says satisfied with 1997 so far.

text.p: Newly merged Swedish/U.S. car safety equipment maker Autoliv Inc said on Monday that it was safisfied overall with its performance in the first half of 1997 and since its merger two months ago.

Autoliv, formed by merging Sweden's Autoliv AB and Morton International's car safety unit ASP on May 1, posted a three percent rise in sales in the first half and profit after financial items of $177 million against $161 million a year ago.
"We are satisfied with the outcome of the first two months of the operations and for the first two quarters," chairman and chief executive Gunnar Bark told a telephone conference.
"You are never satisfied with all aspects of a company ...but so far I would not say we are disappointed in a significant way in any aspect of the combined company."
Bark said the merger was a very good combination and there were good synergies out of it.
He said the costs of restructuring the new company would not be released until after the third quarter results on October 22.
"Longterm the real benefits will come from the top line synergies," he said.
Autoliv shares closed 2.5 higher at 295.5 crowns in Stockholm on Monday.
